key_insight: In de novo Parkinson’s disease, cognitive decline appears to be driven by faster neurodegeneration on top of pre-existing white matter hyperintensity–related vascular vulnerability, rather than by faster WMH accumulation itself.
clinical_relevance: This suggests that both brain atrophy patterns and vascular burden may help identify patients at higher risk of multidomain progression in Parkinson’s disease.
method: Longitudinal PPMI cohort of newly diagnosed, untreated PD participants who were cognitively normal at baseline.
Linear mixed-effects models assessed cognitive, motor, and imaging trajectories over at least 3 years.
Mixed-effects models tested whether baseline WMH burden and a decline-related atrophy pattern predicted later multidomain clinical progression.
evidence_signal: Among 350 participants, 58 converted to cognitive decline and 292 remained stable; converters showed faster decline across cognitive and non-cognitive domains, with significant associations reported at q<0.05 for multiple outcomes.
watch_item: Findings are observational and cohort-specific, so the temporal and predictive value of WMH burden and atrophy patterns should be validated before use in routine risk stratification.
paper_title: Vascular and neurodegenerative contributions to cognitive decline and multidomain progression in de novo Parkinsons disease
